label: copy phase, mid-sequence, input echo is d/i/y/h/p
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter steps), only when the fed-back input token is not a first occurrence, and almost entirely when that input is d, i, y, h or p (d and i carry about 70% of the mass). It is concentrated mid-copy at recall_idx 3-5 and to_go 3-5, peaking at absolute step t=12, so it is mostly found in long sequences (L=9 holds 64% of the mass). Activations are strongest for d/i input when the next output is a (top examples look like ...d -> a). The predicate captures about 80% of activations and mass, but precision is only about 2%: most steps that match these conditions stay silent, and adding out_tok, L or exact position conditions raises precision only to about 17% while recall falls sharply. So the gating context is only partly captured. It does not fire on letters like l, r, m, s, j, g, v, or on digits as input.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=y (+5.48), phase=2 & in_tok=d (+5.30), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+5.27), phase=2 & in_tok=i (+4.91), phase=2 & out_tok=a (+3.93), phase=2 & in_tok=p (+3.74). Lower it: prev_tok=c (-2.89), orig5=f (-2.30), recall_idx=1 (-2.07), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.07).
